title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: A Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator-metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task, reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, precise execution accounting, representative validator-trace excerpt, quantitative analysis, diagnostic interpretation, and artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments required to estimate validator coverage and repair utility.

sections.introduction:
Reliable automated NetOps requires not only powerful generative models but also deterministic acceptance mechanisms that prevent silent, harmful, or wrong-but-plausible changes. A common operational architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): an LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic validator checks mechanistic constraints, and—when necessary—a repair module synthesizes corrections or triggers human review. Prior system work and architectural proposals motivate GVR insertion for safety and auditability, yet systematic, preregistered measurements of validator coverage (false-positive/false-negative rates), detection latency, and predictive usefulness for end-to-end guarded success remain underdeveloped. We preregistered study AC-2026-03 to measure whether a multidimensional validator-metric suite (coverage, FP-rate, FN-rate, mean detection latency, operational-impact proxy) predicts agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate.

We executed a paired confirmatory design under shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task a single initial candidate was sampled and reused for both baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator and permitted repair) conditions. Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise downstream from validator-triggered repair. Our experiment produced a degenerate but artifact-grounded outcome: every sampled initial candidate passed the deterministic validator and no repairs were applied. The manuscript documents preregistered design choices, exact execution accounting, representative validator traces, statistical outcomes, and concrete, artifact-supported next-step preregistered arms (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) needed to produce estimable validator metrics. Our contribution is (1) a fully preregistered, archived confirmatory run with transparent accounting; (2) an exact report of a ceiling outcome with diagnostic analysis grounded in archived artifacts; and (3) concrete, reproducible prescriptions for follow-up experiments that remove the observed degeneracy.
sections.related_work:
Architectural and experimental evidence motivates verifier layers inside GVR pipelines but does not establish comprehensive empirical coverage for NetOps validators. Convergent-correctness and GVR proposals in the coding and regulated-systems literature describe generate–verify–repair loops that detect mechanically checkable defects and support deterministic acceptance criteria [1]. Recent NetOps/AIOps benchmarks show substantive failure modes—ticket noise, false premises, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that complicate end-to-end automation and motivate verifier insertion [2],[3]. System reports and prototype studies propose self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair to reduce silent or action-triggering failures in tool-augmented LLM systems [4]. Surveys of LLMs for telecommunications and NetOps summarize adaptation, verification trade-offs, and the need to measure verification cost and coverage, motivating metricized evaluation of verifier utility [5].

These records collectively argue that verifier layers can reduce certain classes of error, but none supplies a standardized, empirically estimable validator-metric suite for NetOps GVR flows. Our preregistered study was designed to begin filling that measurement gap under strict preregistration and archived-execution practices. We treat the cited works as architectural motivation and methodological precedent rather than as empirical proof that NetOps validators provide comprehensive coverage across realistic, heterogeneous production scenarios.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The study was preregistered (AC-2026-03) and archived (preregistration_sha256 = de37b485421cb0895a98df38b6b3baad1dc7c13c81065e3d8240d2a94a0ff844). Key preregistered elements: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared model = gpt-5-mini; task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistered primary test was an exact two-sided McNemar test with paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Task bank and deterministic task generation. Tasks were drawn deterministically from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1) at 'very_hard' and 'extreme' difficulty settings. Each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, compact intent, allowed_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence. The task-manifest and representative task entries (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) are archived and include generation_seed values that produce reproducible required answers for the deterministic generator.

Model and sampling configuration. The declared execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", requested_model = "gpt-5-mini", max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1, provider = "openai_responses", and temperature = null. We explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is recorded by the execution artifact and is not evidence of deterministic provider-side sampling; null/unset does not imply temperature = 0. The adapter audit confirms hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with one shared initial generation per pair and with generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate.

Validator, scoring, and repair policy. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator implements mechanistic intent-constraint checks and emits per-episode fields: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair_provider_trace fields when repairs occur. The preregistered binary scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation uses validator.valid as the success label for the confirmatory estimand. The pipeline permits at most one repair call when validator.valid is false; repair traces would be archived under repair_provider_trace_path.

Inclusion/exclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. Exclusion rules (preregistered): exact-duplicate outputs (identical SHA-256) cause automatic exclusion and deterministic replacement; near-duplicate tasks (embedding cosine similarity > 0.95) cause deterministic replacement. Contamination and missingness checking are implemented and archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv and analysis/missingness_summary.csv). The missingness plan enforced complete-pair analysis; no manual retries were permitted (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1). The run produced no exclusions and no missing episodes (complete_pair_count = 200).

Power and analysis plan. The power plan targeted detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 at α = 0.05 with ~80% power under conservative baseline p = 0.50 and various within-pair correlations; bootstrap stability checks were preregistered (planning recommendation 1,000 resamples). The confirmatory analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor, exact McNemar two-sided test, and paired bootstrap percentile CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) as recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter completed the preregistered run: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair). Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json): hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. No contamination exclusions occurred (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty) and no episodes were missing (analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 200).

Primary confirmatory outcome. The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0), guarded successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. These numeric artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and their hashes are recorded in the execution manifest.

Representative validator-trace excerpt. To illustrate validator semantics and why no repairs were triggered, we reproduce verbatim key fields from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json (representative pair):
  - pair_id: pair-000004
  - normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
  - parsed_command_count: 4
  - required_command_count: 4
  - observed_touched_field_count: 3
  - valid: true
  - repair_applied: false
  - validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
  - validator_version: 5.0

The same pattern (validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false) holds for every archived episode; repair_provider_trace_path is null in all scoring artifacts. Representative per-episode raw responses and validator traces are stored in execution/responses and execution/scoring and can be inspected for all pairs (execution/raw_results.jsonl). The analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg) record and visualize the degenerate distribution (point mass at 0.00).

Exploratory diagnostics. Because repair_applied = false for all episodes, per-validator FP/FN and repair-latency distributions are degenerate and uninformative for estimating coverage. The archived artifacts nonetheless permit re-scoring under alternative definitions (e.g., semantic intent mismatch heuristics) or re-execution under modified preregistered arms (fault injection, multi-sample draws) without manual editing of the original run artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Diagnostic interpretation of the ceiling outcome. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline and guarded conditions evaluated the identical initial candidate per pair; therefore any paired difference could only arise from downstream validator-triggered repair. The degenerate all-valid outcome has three artifact-grounded determinants visible in the archive: (1) the synthetic generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with fixed generation_seed per task) produced candidates satisfying the validator's mechanistic constraints for the recorded seeds; (2) the one-sample-per-task sampling regime removed generator variability as a source of disagreements; and (3) the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic checks but cannot detect some classes of semantic intent misalignment that are correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent. These elements together explain why no repairs occurred and the confirmatory test could not detect the preregistered 10-percentage-point improvement.

Implications for validator evaluation. The result does not imply that validators are unnecessary; rather it shows that (a) paired shared_initial_candidate designs isolate repair effects cleanly but risk single-sample ceilings when generator and validator align, and (b) deterministic validators that check mechanistic constraints can produce degenerate outcome distributions if the task bank and sampling produce high baseline correctness. To estimate validator FP/FN and repair value we require experimental arms that produce measurable initial invalidity or generator variability; we prescribe three concrete, artifact-supported follow-ups below.

Artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments. All suggested arms can be implemented within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter and deterministic task-generation machinery archived in the execution bundle:
  1) Fault-injection arm (preregistered): deterministically inject a controlled set of faults into reference answers for a fraction f of tasks (syntactic errors, configuration-logic faults, semantic-intent swaps). This creates measurable baseline invalidity and enables estimation of validator FN and guarded repair utility. The execution bundle already contains deterministic replacement and contamination rules to implement this arm reproducibly.
  2) Multi-sample stochastic generation: set initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task and allow the guarded pipeline to accept any validator-approved candidate among the k draws or to perform repair. Recording seeds and provider-call traces will reveal generator variability and allow empirical estimation of validator coverage across draws.
  3) Multi-validator and multi-model comparison: add at least one alternative validator implementation and at least one additional model family. Comparing validator coverage and repair outcomes across validators and models will quantify sensitivity to validator design choices and to model sampling behaviour. Each arm should retain preregistered paired estimands and contamination controls and record provider-call audits as in the present run.

Threats to validity and practical constraints. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate intentionally isolates downstream effects but increases ceiling risk, and the recorded temperature = null/unset does not guarantee deterministic sampling. Construct validity: validator.valid operationalizes mechanistic correctness but may not reflect semantic intent alignment. External validity: synthetic task bank, single-model execution (gpt-5-mini), and one deterministic validator limit generalization to heterogeneous production networks and other model families. Conclusion validity: with baseline success = 1.0 the primary estimand exhibits zero variance, rendering inferential claims about validator benefit impossible from this run alone. These threats are artifact-documented (analysis/missingness_summary.csv, deterministic_reconciliation.json) and motivate the prescribed follow-ups.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, the sampled gpt-5-mini seeds, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. This artifact-grounded result is reproducible from the archived bundle. We publish exact execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and provide concrete, preregistered experiment prescriptions (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) that are required to produce estimable validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions. Future work should implement these preregistered arms to measure validator coverage, repair utility, and operational-impact prediction capability.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
